sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam evam uktvā vacanaṃ maharṣis; tapasvimadhye sahitaṃ suhṛdbhiḥ āmantrya dhaumyaṃ sahitāṃś ca pārthāṃs; tataḥ pratasthe diśam uttarāṃ saḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having spoken thus, that great sage, in the company of ascetics and friends, took leave of Dhaumya and the sons of Pṛthā together, and then set out towards the northern direction.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca vasatsv atha dvaitavane pāṇḍaveṣu mahātmasu anukīrṇaṃ mahāraṇyaṃ brāhmaṇaiḥ samapadyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the great-souled Pāṇḍavas were dwelling in the Dvaita forest, that great wilderness became filled with brahmanas on all sides.

sanskrit: īryamāṇena satataṃ brahmaghoṣeṇa sarvataḥ brahmalokasamaṃ puṇyam āsīd dvaitavanaṃ saraḥ
english: Constantly resounding from all quarters with the chanting of Vedic hymns, the sacred lake of Dvaita forest became equal to the realm of Brahmā in its holiness.

sanskrit: yajuṣām ṛcāṃ ca sāmnāṃ ca gadyānāṃ caiva sarvaśaḥ āsīd uccāryamāṇānāṃ nisvano hṛdayaṃgamaḥ
english: The resonant sound of Yajus, Ric, Sāman, and prose recitations being chanted on all sides was deeply pleasing to the heart.

sanskrit: jyāghoṣaḥ pāṇḍaveyānāṃ brahmaghoṣaś ca dhīmatām saṃsṛṣṭaṃ brahmaṇā kṣatraṃ bhūya eva vyarocata
english: The twang of the Pāṇḍavas' bowstrings and the Vedic chanting of the wise ones mingled together, and the Kṣatriya joined with Brahman shone all the more brilliantly.

sanskrit: athābravīd bako dālbhyo dharmarājaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram saṃdhyāṃ kaunteyam āsīnam ṛṣibhiḥ parivāritam
english: Then Baka of the Dālbhya lineage addressed Dharmarāja Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, who was seated at twilight surrounded by sages.

sanskrit: paśya dvaitavane pārtha brāhmaṇānāṃ tapasvinām homavelāṃ kuruśreṣṭha saṃprajvalitapāvakām
english: "Behold, O Pārtha, O foremost of the Kurus, the oblation-hour of the ascetic brahmanas in the Dvaita forest, with their sacred fires blazing brightly.

sanskrit: caranti dharmaṃ puṇye 'smiṃs tvayā guptā dhṛtavratāḥ bhṛgavo 'ṅgirasaś caiva vāsiṣṭhāḥ kāśyapaiḥ saha
english: Protected by you and firm in their vows, the descendants of Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Vasiṣṭha, and the Kashyapas practice righteousness in this sacred place.

sanskrit: āgastyāś ca mahābhāgā ātreyāś cottamavratāḥ sarvasya jagataḥ śreṣṭhā brāhmaṇāḥ saṃgatās tvayā
english: The illustrious descendants of Agastya and the Ātreyas of highest vows — brahmanas who are the best in all the world — have gathered around you.

sanskrit: idaṃ tu vacanaṃ pārtha śṛṇv ekāgramanā mama bhrātṛbhiḥ saha kaunteya yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi kaurava
english: "But hear this word of mine, O Pārtha, O son of Kuntī, O Kaurava, with concentrated mind, together with your brothers, as I speak it to you.

sanskrit: brahma kṣatreṇa saṃsṛṣṭaṃ kṣatraṃ ca brahmaṇā saha udīrṇau dahataḥ śatrūn vanānīvāgnimārutau
english: The Brahman united with the Kṣatriya, and the Kṣatriya united with the Brahman — when both are roused, they burn enemies like fire and wind burn forests.

sanskrit: nābrāhmaṇas tāta ciraṃ bubhūṣed; icchann imaṃ lokam amuṃ ca jetum vinītadharmārtham apetamohaṃ; labdhvā dvijaṃ nudati nṛpaḥ sapatnān
english: A king who is without a brahmana, dear one, cannot long endure; desiring to conquer this world and the next, having learned dharma and artha, freed from delusion — having obtained a twice-born, a king drives away his enemies.

sanskrit: caran naiḥśreyasaṃ dharmaṃ prajāpālanakāritam nādhyagacchad balir loke tīrtham anyatra vai dvijāt
english: Practicing the highest dharma and dedicated to the protection of his subjects, Bali found no sacred ford in the world other than the twice-born.

sanskrit: anūnam āsīd asurasya kāmair; vairocaneḥ śrīr api cākṣayāsīt labdhvā mahīṃ brāhmaṇasaṃprayogāt; teṣv ācaran duṣṭam ato vyanaśyat
english: The desires of that asura were fulfilled and the prosperity of Vairocana was inexhaustible — having obtained the earth through association with brahmanas; but having acted wickedly toward them, he perished on that account.

sanskrit: nābrāhmaṇaṃ bhūmir iyaṃ sabhūtir; varṇaṃ dvitīyaṃ bhajate cirāya samudranemir namate tu tasmai; yaṃ brāhmaṇaḥ śāsti nayair vinītaḥ
english: This earth with its creatures does not long serve the second varna if without a brahmana; the sea-girdled earth bows to him whom a well-instructed brahmana guides with righteous counsel.

sanskrit: kuñjarasyeva saṃgrāme 'parigṛhyāṅkuśagraham brāhmaṇair viprahīṇasya kṣatrasya kṣīyate balam
english: Just as an elephant in battle whose mahout with the goad has let go of the hold — so the strength of the Kṣatriya deprived of brahmanas wanes away.

sanskrit: brahmaṇy anupamā dṛṣṭiḥ kṣātram apratimaṃ balam tau yadā carataḥ sārdham atha lokaḥ prasīdati
english: In the Brahman there is unparalleled wisdom; in the Kṣatriya there is unmatched strength. When these two act together, then the world rejoices.

sanskrit: yathā hi sumahān agniḥ kakṣaṃ dahati sānilaḥ tathā dahati rājanyo brāhmaṇena samaṃ ripūn
english: Just as a great fire aided by wind burns dry grass, so a king together with a brahmana burns his enemies.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇebhyo 'tha medhāvī buddhiparyeṣaṇaṃ caret alabdhasya ca lābhāya labdhasya ca vivṛddhaye
english: The wise man should seek the guidance of brahmanas — for the gaining of what has not been gained, and for the increase of what has already been gained.

sanskrit: alabdhalābhāya ca labdhavṛddhaye; yathārhatīrthapratipādanāya yaśasvinaṃ vedavidaṃ vipaścitaṃ; bahuśrutaṃ brāhmaṇam eva vāsaya
english: For the gaining of the ungained and the growth of the gained, for the proper endowment of worthy tirthas — keep near you a brahmana who is illustrious, learned in the Vedas, wise, and widely versed in scripture.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇeṣūttamā vṛttis tava nityaṃ yudhiṣṭhira tena te sarvalokeṣu dīpyate prathitaṃ yaśaḥ
english: Your conduct toward brahmanas is always excellent, O Yudhiṣṭhira; because of that your wide-spread fame blazes forth in all the worlds.

sanskrit: tatas te brāhmaṇāḥ sarve bakaṃ dālbhyam apūjayan yudhiṣṭhire stūyamāne bhūyaḥ sumanaso 'bhavan
english: Then all those brahmanas honored Baka of the Dālbhya lineage, and as Yudhiṣṭhira was praised, they became even more pleased in their hearts.

sanskrit: dvaipāyano nāradaś ca jāmadagnyaḥ pṛthuśravāḥ indradyumno bhālukiś ca kṛtacetāḥ sahasrapāt
english: Dvaipāyana, Nārada, Jāmadagnya, Pṛthu-shravas, Indradyumna, Bhāluki, Kritachetas, Sahasrapāt —

sanskrit: karṇaśravāś ca muñjaś ca lavaṇāśvaś ca kāśyapaḥ hārītaḥ sthūṇakarṇaś ca agniveśyo 'tha śaunakaḥ
english: — Karnashravas, Munja, Lavanashva of the Kaśyapa lineage, Harita, Sthūṇākarṇa, Agniveśa, and Śaunaka —

sanskrit: ṛtavāk ca suvāk caiva bṛhadaśva ṛtāvasuḥ ūrdhvaretā vṛṣāmitraḥ suhotro hotravāhanaḥ
english: — Ritavak, Suvak, Bṛhadaśva, Ritavasu, Urdhvareta, Vrishamitra, Suhotra, and Hotravāhana —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo brāhmaṇāḥ saṃśitavratāḥ ajātaśatrum ānarcuḥ puraṃdaram ivarṣayaḥ
english: — these and many other brahmanas of sharpened vows praised Ajātaśatru as sages praise Purandara.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vanagatāḥ pārthāḥ sāyāhne saha kṛṣṇayā upaviṣṭāḥ kathāś cakrur duḥkhaśokaparāyaṇāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the Pārthas, who had gone to the forest, sat down in the evening together with Kṛṣṇā (Draupadī) and engaged in conversation, absorbed in grief and sorrow.

sanskrit: priyā ca darśanīyā ca paṇḍitā ca pativratā tataḥ kṛṣṇā dharmarājam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Kṛṣṇā — beloved, beautiful, wise, and devoted to her husband — spoke these words to Dharmarāja.

sanskrit: na nūnaṃ tasya pāpasya duḥkham asmāsu kiṃ cana vidyate dhārtarāṣṭrasya nṛśaṃsasya durātmanaḥ
english: "Surely that sinful, cruel, evil-souled son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra feels no pain at all at what has befallen us.

sanskrit: yas tvāṃ rājan mayā sārdham ajinaiḥ prativāsitam bhrātṛbhiś ca tathā sarvair nābhyabhāṣata kiṃ cana vanaṃ prasthāpya duṣṭātmā nānvatapyata durmatiḥ
english: "That evil-minded, wicked-souled wretch, O king, sent you away to the forest clad in deerskins along with me and all your brothers, and said not a word — and he did not repent.

sanskrit: āyasaṃ hṛdayaṃ nūnaṃ tasya duṣkṛtakarmaṇaḥ yas tvāṃ dharmaparaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ rūkṣāṇy aśrāvayat tadā
english: "Surely the heart of that evil-doer is made of iron — the one who made you, the foremost upholder of dharma, hear such harsh words at that time.

sanskrit: sukhocitam aduḥkhārhaṃ durātmā sasuhṛdgaṇaḥ īdṛśaṃ duḥkham ānīya modate pāpapūruṣaḥ
english: "That evil-souled wicked man, with his band of allies, having brought such suffering upon one accustomed to ease and undeserving of pain, now rejoices.

sanskrit: caturṇām eva pāpānām aśru vai nāpatat tadā tvayi bhārata niṣkrānte vanāyājinavāsasi
english: "When you, O Bhārata, departed for the forest to dwell in deerskins, the eyes of only those four sinners shed no tears.

sanskrit: duryodhanasya karṇasya śakuneś ca durātmanaḥ durbhrātus tasya cograsya tathā duḥśāsanasya ca
english: "Those four were Duryodhana, Karṇa, the evil-souled Śakuni, and that fierce wicked-brother Duḥśāsana.

sanskrit: itareṣāṃ tu sarveṣāṃ kurūṇāṃ kurusattama duḥkhenābhiparītānāṃ netrebhyaḥ prāpataj jalam
english: "But from the eyes of all the other Kurus, O foremost of the Kurus, who were overwhelmed with grief, water fell down in tears.

sanskrit: idaṃ ca śayanaṃ dṛṣṭvā yac cāsīt te purātanam śocāmi tvāṃ mahārāja duḥkhānarhaṃ sukhocitam
english: "Seeing this bed now and remembering what was yours before, O great king, I grieve for you — you who are undeserving of suffering and accustomed to ease.

sanskrit: dāntaṃ yac ca sabhāmadhye āsanaṃ ratnabhūṣitam dṛṣṭvā kuśabṛsīṃ cemāṃ śoko māṃ rundhayaty ayam
english: "Seeing the ivory gem-adorned seat that was yours in the assembly-hall and now seeing this grass mat — this grief overwhelms me.

sanskrit: yad apaśyaṃ sabhāyāṃ tvāṃ rājabhiḥ parivāritam tac ca rājann apaśyantyāḥ kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: "I who once saw you in the assembly surrounded by kings — now not seeing that, O king — what peace can there be in my heart?

sanskrit: yā tvāhaṃ candanādigdham apaśyaṃ sūryavarcasam sā tvā paṅkamalādigdhaṃ dṛṣṭvā muhyāmi bhārata
english: "I who used to see you anointed with sandalwood paste and radiant as the sun — now seeing you smeared with mud and dust, I am bewildered, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yā vai tvā kauśikair vastraiḥ śubhrair bahudhanaiḥ purā dṛṣṭavaty asmi rājendra sā tvāṃ paśyāmi cīriṇam
english: "I who formerly saw you, O lord of kings, dressed in silk garments, white and richly woven — now I see you wearing bark garments.

sanskrit: yac ca tad rukmapātrībhir brāhmaṇebhyaḥ sahasraśaḥ hriyate te gṛhād annaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ sārvakāmikam
english: "That food, prepared and fulfilling every desire, which was carried from your house in thousands of golden vessels to be given to brahmanas —

sanskrit: yatīnām agṛhāṇāṃ te tathaiva gṛhamedhinām dīyate bhojanaṃ rājann atīva guṇavat prabho tac ca rājann apaśyantyāḥ kā śāntir hṛdayasya me
english: "— that food of exceeding excellence which was given to wandering ascetics and to householders alike, O king, O lord — not seeing that now, O king, what peace can there be in my heart?

sanskrit: yāṃs te bhrātṝn mahārāja yuvāno mṛṣṭakuṇḍalāḥ abhojayanta mṛṣṭānnaiḥ sūdāḥ paramasaṃskṛtaiḥ
english: "Those brothers of yours, O great king — young men wearing bright earrings — your cooks used to feed with the most perfectly prepared and pure food —

sanskrit: sarvāṃs tān adya paśyāmi vane vanyena jīvataḥ aduḥkhārhān manuṣyendra nopaśāmyati me manaḥ
english: "— all of them I now see living in the forest on forest fare, though they are undeserving of such hardship, O lord of men. My mind does not find peace.

sanskrit: bhīmasenam imaṃ cāpi duḥkhitaṃ vanavāsinam dhyāyantaṃ kiṃ na manyus te prāpte kāle vivardhate
english: "And seeing Bhīmasena here, afflicted and dwelling in the forest, brooding in thought — why does your anger not grow, now that the time has come?

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ hi karmāṇi svayaṃ kurvāṇam acyuta sukhārhaṃ duḥkhitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "Seeing Bhīmasena, who is deserving of ease, doing all tasks himself and now afflicted — O steadfast one, why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: satkṛtaṃ vividhair yānair vastrair uccāvacais tathā taṃ te vanagataṃ dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "He who was honored with various conveyances and garments of high and low quality alike — seeing him now gone to the forest, why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: kurūn api hi yaḥ sarvān hantum utsahate prabhuḥ tvatprasādaṃ pratīkṣaṃs tu sahate 'yaṃ vṛkodaraḥ
english: "This Vṛkodara, who is capable of slaying all the Kurus, endures only awaiting your favor, O lord.

sanskrit: yo 'rjunenārjunas tulyo dvibāhur bahubāhunā śarātisarge śīghratvāt kālāntakayamopamaḥ
english: "He who, though having only two arms, is equal to Arjuna of many arms in the speed of his arrow-release — a man like Yama and the Destroyer of Time —

sanskrit: yasya śastrapratāpena praṇatāḥ sarvapārthivāḥ yajñe tava mahārāja brāhmaṇān upatasthire
english: "— by whose weapon-prowess all the kings were made to bow down and waited upon the brahmanas at your sacrifice, O great king —

sanskrit: tam imaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ pūjitaṃ devadānavaiḥ dhyāyantam arjunaṃ dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "— seeing this tiger among men, Arjuna, honored by gods and demons, now brooding in thought — why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā vanagataṃ pārtham aduḥkhārhaṃ sukhocitam na ca te vardhate manyus tena muhyāmi bhārata
english: "Seeing Pārtha gone to the forest, undeserving of sorrow and accustomed to ease — your anger does not grow; by this I am bewildered, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: yo devāṃś ca manuṣyāṃś ca sarpāṃś caikaratho 'jayat taṃ te vanagataṃ dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "He who, with a single chariot, conquered gods, men, and serpents — seeing him gone to the forest, why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: yo yānair adbhutākārair hayair nāgaiś ca saṃvṛtaḥ prasahya vittāny ādatta pārthivebhyaḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: "He who, surrounded by conveyances of wondrous form and horses and elephants, forcibly seized wealth from kings — that scorcher of foes —

sanskrit: kṣipaty ekena vegena pañca bāṇaśatāni yaḥ taṃ te vanagataṃ dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "— he who shoots five hundred arrows in a single swift release — seeing him gone to the forest, why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: śyāmaṃ bṛhantaṃ taruṇaṃ carmiṇām uttamaṃ raṇe nakulaṃ te vane dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "Seeing Nakula, dark-complexioned, tall, young, supreme among swordsmen in battle, now gone to the forest — why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: darśanīyaṃ ca śūraṃ ca mādrīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhira sahadevaṃ vane dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "Seeing the handsome and heroic son of Mādrī, Sahadeva, gone to the forest, O Yudhiṣṭhira — why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: drupadasya kule jātāṃ snuṣāṃ pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ māṃ te vanagatāṃ dṛṣṭvā kasmān manyur na vardhate
english: "Seeing me, born in the lineage of Drupada, the daughter-in-law of the great-souled Pāṇḍu, now gone to the forest — why does your anger not grow?

sanskrit: nūnaṃ ca tava naivāsti manyur bharatasattama yat te bhrātṝṃś ca māṃ caiva dṛṣṭvā na vyathate manaḥ
english: "Surely you have no anger at all, O foremost of the Bhāratas — for seeing your brothers and me in this state, your mind is not moved to pain.

sanskrit: na nirmanyuḥ kṣatriyo 'sti loke nirvacanaṃ smṛtam tad adya tvayi paśyāmi kṣatriye viparītavat
english: "It is the established saying that there is no Kṣatriya without anger; yet today I see the opposite of that in you, a Kṣatriya.

sanskrit: yo na darśayate tejaḥ kṣatriyaḥ kāla āgate sarvabhūtāni taṃ pārtha sadā paribhavanty uta
english: "The Kṣatriya who does not display his fiery energy when the time comes — all creatures ever despise him, O Pārtha.

sanskrit: tat tvayā na kṣamā kāryā śatrūn prati kathaṃ cana tejasaiva hi te śakyā nihantuṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ
english: "Therefore you should in no way practice forbearance toward your enemies; it is only through your fiery energy that they can be slain — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: tathaiva yaḥ kṣamākāle kṣatriyo nopaśāmyati apriyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ so 'mutreha ca naśyati
english: "And likewise, the Kṣatriya who does not calm himself when the time for forbearance has come becomes disliked by all creatures and perishes both here and hereafter."

sanskrit: draupady uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam prahlādasya ca saṃvādaṃ baler vairocanasya ca
english: Draupadī said: "On this point they also cite this ancient story — the dialogue of Prahlāda and Bali the son of Vairocana.

sanskrit: asurendraṃ mahāprājñaṃ dharmāṇām āgatāgamam baliḥ papraccha daityendraṃ prahlādaṃ pitaraṃ pituḥ
english: "Bali questioned Prahlāda, lord of the asuras, greatly wise, acquainted with the coming and going of dharmas — Prahlāda, lord of the daityas, his father's father.

sanskrit: kṣamā svic chreyasī tāta utāho teja ity uta etan me saṃśayaṃ tāta yathāvad brūhi pṛcchate
english: "'Is forbearance better, dear one, or is fiery energy? This is my doubt, dear one — tell me truly as I ask you.'

sanskrit: śreyo yad atra dharmajña brūhi me tad asaṃśayam kariṣyāmi hi tat sarvaṃ yathāvad anuśāsanam
english: "'What is the superior path here, O knower of dharma — tell me that without doubt. I will do all of it according to your instruction.'

sanskrit: tasmai provāca tat sarvam evaṃ pṛṣṭaḥ pitāmahaḥ sarvaniścayavit prājñaḥ saṃśayaṃ paripṛcchate
english: "Thus questioned by him, the grandsire, wise and knowing all conclusions, spoke to him in full as he inquired about this doubt.

sanskrit: prahlāda uvāca na śreyaḥ satataṃ tejo na nityaṃ śreyasī kṣamā iti tāta vijānīhi dvayam etad asaṃśayam
english: "Prahlāda said: 'Fiery energy is not always better, nor is forbearance always better — know this, dear one: both of these, without doubt.

sanskrit: yo nityaṃ kṣamate tāta bahūn doṣān sa vindati bhṛtyāḥ paribhavanty enam udāsīnās tathaiva ca
english: "'He who always forbears, dear one, incurs many faults: servants despise him, and indifferent persons likewise.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtāni cāpy asya na namante kadā cana tasmān nityaṃ kṣamā tāta paṇḍitair apavāditā
english: "'And all creatures never bow to him at any time; therefore perpetual forbearance, dear one, is condemned by the wise.

sanskrit: avajñāya hi taṃ bhṛtyā bhajante bahudoṣatām ādātuṃ cāsya vittāni prārthayante 'lpacetasaḥ
english: "'For servants, despising him, go on to great misconduct and the feeble-minded seek to take away his wealth.

sanskrit: yānaṃ vastrāṇy alaṃkārāñ śayanāny āsanāni ca bhojanāny atha pānāni sarvopakaraṇāni ca
english: "'Conveyances, garments, ornaments, beds and seats, food and drink, and all his equipment —

sanskrit: ādadīrann adhikṛtā yathākāmam acetasaḥ pradiṣṭāni ca deyāni na dadyur bhartṛśāsanāt
english: "'— his officials, mindless, would take as they please, and what has been prescribed to be given they would not give in accordance with the master's command.

sanskrit: na cainaṃ bhartṛpūjābhiḥ pūjayanti kadā cana avajñānaṃ hi loke 'smin maraṇād api garhitam
english: "'And they would never honor him with the honors due to a master; for in this world contempt is even more condemned than death.

sanskrit: kṣamiṇaṃ tādṛśaṃ tāta bruvanti kaṭukāny api preṣyāḥ putrāś ca bhṛtyāś ca tathodāsīnavṛttayaḥ
english: "'To such a forbearing man, dear one, even servants, sons, subordinates, and those who behave indifferently speak bitter words.

sanskrit: apy asya dārān icchanti paribhūya kṣamāvataḥ dārāś cāsya pravartante yathākāmam acetasaḥ
english: "'They even desire his wives after showing contempt for the forbearing man, and his wives, mindless, behave as they please.

sanskrit: tathā ca nityam uditā yadi svalpam apīśvarāt daṇḍam arhanti duṣyanti duṣṭāś cāpy apakurvate
english: "'And those who are always rising — if they deserve even a small punishment from the lord, the wicked ones transgress and do harm.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo nityaṃ doṣāḥ kṣamāvatām atha vairocane doṣān imān viddhy akṣamāvatām
english: "'These and many others are the perpetual faults of those who are always forbearing. Now, O son of Vairocana, know the faults of those who are without forbearance.

sanskrit: asthāne yadi vā sthāne satataṃ rajasāvṛtaḥ kruddho daṇḍān praṇayati vividhān svena tejasā
english: "'Whether in the right place or the wrong, constantly overcome by passion, in anger he inflicts various punishments through his own fiery energy.
